root_cause.text: A lack of serialization in the `hci_dma_dequeue_xfer()` function allows concurrent execution of the DMA ring dequeue path during multiple simultaneous transfer timeouts, resulting in a race condition when stopping and restarting the DMA ring.
root_cause.evidence: The patch introduces and initializes `control_mutex` in `struct i3c_hci` and uses `guard(mutex)(&hci->control_mutex)` at the beginning of `hci_dma_dequeue_xfer()` to serialize the function against itself.

commit 9ad9a52cce2828d932ae9495181e3d6414f72c07
Author: Nicolas Pitre <npitre@baylibre.com>
Date:   Wed Nov 11 17:05:10 2020 -0500

    i3c/master: introduce the mipi-i3c-hci driver
    
    This adds basic support for hardware implementing the MIPI I3C HCI
    specification. This driver is currently limited by the capabilities
    of the I3C subsystem, meaning things like scheduled commands,
    auto-commands and NCM mode are not yet supported.
    
    This supports version 1.0 of the MIPI I3C
bic_trace_step.reason: The `hci_dma_dequeue_xfer()` function (lines 447-505) lacks any serialization (such as a mutex or spinlock) around the ring stop and restart sequence (specifically, the writes to `RING_CONTROL` with `RING_CTRL_ABORT` and `RING_CTRL_ENABLE`). This allows concurrent execution of the dequeue path during multiple simultaneous transfer timeouts, leading to a race condition when stopping and restarting the DMA ring.

bic_trace_step.reason: The `hci_dma_dequeue_xfer()` function (lines 434-489) lacks any serialization (such as a spinlock or mutex) to prevent concurrent execution when multiple transfers timeout simultaneously. Specifically, it writes to `RING_CONTROL` to abort and enable the ring (lines 441 and 486) and modifies the ring descriptors (lines 453-477) without holding any lock, leading to a race condition.
